item.title: A Gentle Introduction to Smooth Manifolds
item.description: Abstract. A smooth manifold is a space that may be globally curved or topologically complicated while remaining locally indistinguishable from Euclidean space. This post introduces this concept from first principles. We begin with topology, charts, transition maps, and atlases; then define smooth functions and smooth maps without assuming that the manifold sits inside a larger Euclidean space. From there, we construct tangent and cotangent spaces, differentials, vector fields, integral curves, flows, and Lie brackets. The sphere serves as a recurring example, allowing each abstract definition to be compared with familiar geometry. The central theme is that coordinates make calculations possible, while compatibility under coordinate changes makes the resulting mathematics intrinsic.
